stem:
The diagram shows Nupur at a wall switch after washing; water droplets are still on her hand near the switch.

Which claim about safety is correct?

options.text: She may touch the switch with wet hands.
She must not touch any switch later, even with dry hands during normal use.
She should dry her hands before touching the switch.
She may touch the switch with wet hands if the switch looks cool and shows no heating.

teacher.key_rationale: Do not touch switches or plugs with wet hands; dry first. Wet contact is unsafe even if the switch looks cool. Normal dry-hand use of an intact switch is not banned forever.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source resistance-cylinder circuit into a wall switch with a wet hand approaching.
